task: Build stopwatch widget API for spawning multiple independent stopwatches
summary: Created full CRUD + control API for multiple stopwatches with JSON file persistence, following existing iHIM patterns (tasks, notes). Endpoints support spawning, starting, stopping, resetting, lap recording, and deleting stopwatches.

api_endpoints.description: Get all stopwatches with their current state
Create (spawn) a new stopwatch with optional label
Start the stopwatch (sets is_running=true, records started_at)
Stop the stopwatch (calculates and accumulates elapsed_ms)
Reset stopwatch to zero (stops if running)
Record current lap time without stopping

stopwatch_object.label: string (optional name, empty string default)
stopwatch_object.started_at: ISO8601 string or null (set when running)

lap_response.lap_ms: integer (current total elapsed including running time)

handoff_notes: @frontend-dev: The stopwatch API is ready. Key implementation notes: (1) Click + button -> POST /api/stopwatches to spawn new stopwatch, (2) For running stopwatches, calculate DISPLAY time as: elapsed_ms + (Date.now() - Date.parse(started_at)), (3) Use setInterval/requestAnimationFrame for smooth visual timer tick while is_running=true, (4) The API handles persistence - elapsed_ms only gets updated on /stop, so the frontend owns the live display. (5) All control endpoints return the updated stopwatch object.
security_notes: Standard local-only API. No authentication required for localhost iHIM. Label field has max 100 char limit for input validation.

what_went_well: Followed existing patterns from tasks/notes endpoints exactly
Added lap functionality as a bonus feature
Clean separation - API handles persistence, frontend handles visual tick
what_could_improve: Could add a batch create endpoint for spawning multiple at once
Could add optional auto-stop after max duration
Did not implement lap storage - just returns current time
learnings: Stopwatch timing is fundamentally a frontend concern, backend just handles state persistence
The elapsed_ms + started_at pattern allows proper time accumulation across stop/start cycles
